assumptions: The only module-owned deliverables are the s6_owned delivery slots; Makefile, README.md, and the four frozen headers are produced outside module ownership.
s5-ready contracts are owned and provided by the s5 generation stage, not by implementation work packages.
Task-ready contracts use the provider module's owned source files as their mutable implementation boundary because the public headers are s5_frozen.
The server ABI event set, connection-id type, caller-provided storage, and resource limits are authoritative for the application entry point.

contracts.purpose: Expose generated MQTT wire types to codec and session implementation modules.
Expose the stable session interface header.
Expose the stable network interface header.
Expose the module-owned codec implementation boundary.
Expose the module-owned session implementation boundary.
Expose the module-owned network implementation boundary.

decisions.statement: Separate codec, session, network, and server orchestration so each owns its mutable source delivery slots while frozen generated headers remain outside module ownership.
Keep include/mqtt/mqtt_types.h and include/mqtt/mqtt_codec.h as mechanically generated s5 boundaries owned and provided by s5; no implementation module owns them.
Expose runtime implementation boundaries as task-ready contracts whose interface_files are the provider module's mutable owned sources; frozen headers alone cannot serve task gates.
The broker entry point composes session and codec behind the declared server ABI event set with caller-provided storage, connection ids, and bounded output batches.
Protocol violations and transient errors close only the source connection while the server continues serving other clients.

modules.name: Codec
non_goals: Do not own session state or subscription matching.
Do not own network connections or socket I/O.
modules.purpose: Own MQTT 3.1.1 wire codec implementations and consume the generated wire-type and declaration boundaries.
responsibilities: Provide per-message encode/decode implementations for all ten MQTT packets.
Enforce fixed-header flags, remaining-length, UTF-8, and packet-identifier constraints at the codec boundary.
Support client-to-server and server-to-client packet encodings required by the MQTT 3.1.1 specification.

modules.name: Session
non_goals: Do not encode or decode MQTT packets.
modules.purpose: Own MQTT session state and subscription matching.
responsibilities: Maintain per-client session state and subscriptions.
Apply clean-session creation and discard semantics.
Match topic filters against topic names without normalization and remove only exact matching subscriptions.

modules.name: Network Transport
non_goals: Do not interpret MQTT packet contents.
modules.purpose: Own ordered byte-stream transport and output batching.
responsibilities: Accept client network connections and assign connection identifiers.
Deliver ordered, lossless byte streams to the application layer.
Produce bounded output batches per configured resource limits.

modules.name: Server Application
non_goals: Do not implement wire codec bodies.
Do not implement session state internals.
Do not implement raw transport I/O.
modules.purpose: Own the broker entry point that composes codec, session, and network contracts.
responsibilities: Orchestrate MQTT server behavior from connect, bytes, disconnect, and tick events.
Enforce connection ordering, keep-alive, response, forwarding, and protocol-error disconnection semantics.
Forward accepted application messages to matching subscriptions with RETAIN set to zero.

acceptance.outcome: All ten per-message codec implementations compile as C99 and match MQTT 3.1.1 wire vectors.
